meshes.name: glands
meshes.description: Glandular tissue from the scan (approx., from image brightness)

edema.what: Edema: swollen brain tissue around the tumor (bright on FLAIR / T2).
edema.effect: It adds pressure on nearby brain (mass effect) and often causes headaches; steroids can reduce it.

enhancing_tumor.what: Active tumor: the growing rim where contrast leaks through damaged blood vessels.
enhancing_tumor.effect: This is the part doctors measure to judge whether treatment is working (RANO).

necrotic_core.what: Necrotic core: dead tumor tissue in the middle.
necrotic_core.effect: A sign of fast growth, typical of high-grade gliomas; it does not shrink much with treatment.

tumor.what: Breast tumor: tissue that takes up contrast quickly on MRI.
tumor.effect: Its size is used for staging and to follow how it shrinks with chemotherapy.

lesion.effect: Its shape, edges and orientation help tell benign from malignant; a biopsy confirms.

nodule.what: Lung nodule: a small round spot in the lung.
nodule.effect: Most are benign; its size and growth on follow-up CT decide what happens next (Lung-RADS).

possible_extent.what: Possible extent: how deep the tumor could reach.
possible_extent.effect: One image cannot show depth; 9 out of 10 real tumors are shallower than this shell.

glands.what: Glandular tissue: the milk-producing lobules and the ducts that drain them (shown approximately, from how bright the tissue is on the MRI).
glands.effect: Most breast cancers start in the cells lining these ducts and lobules; dense glandular tissue can also hide tumors on mammograms.

fat.what: Fatty tissue: most of the breast's volume, around the glands. Drawn for orientation, not seen on this scan.
fat.effect: Tumors in fatty breasts are easier to see on mammograms than in dense, glandular breasts.

ducts.what: Milk ducts: tubes that carry milk from the lobes to the nipple. Drawn for orientation, not seen on this scan.
ducts.effect: About 8 in 10 breast cancers start in the cells lining the ducts (ductal carcinoma).

lobules.what: Lobes and lobules: 15-20 lobes, each a cluster of small milk-making lobules. Drawn for orientation, not seen on this scan.
lobules.effect: About 1 in 10 breast cancers start here (lobular carcinoma).

ligaments.what: Cooper's ligaments: thin bands that hold the breast's shape. Drawn for orientation, not seen on this scan.
ligaments.effect: A tumor that pulls on them can dimple the skin, a sign doctors look for.

nipple.what: Nipple and areola: where the milk ducts open. Drawn for orientation, not seen on this scan.
nipple.effect: A tumor near the nipple can pull it inwards or cause discharge.

muscle.what: Pectoral (chest) muscle behind the breast. Drawn for orientation, not seen on this scan.
muscle.effect: If a tumor reaches this muscle, surgery and staging change; MRI checks for it.

lymph_nodes.what: Axillary lymph nodes: filters towards the armpit, where breast cancer spreads first. Drawn for orientation, not seen on this scan.
lymph_nodes.effect: Whether they are affected is checked by examination, ultrasound or biopsy; this view does not assess it.

body.what: Outline of the upper body, drawn for orientation. Only the breasts, glands and tumor come from this scan.

classification.label: tumor
classification.display: Breast tumor found (MRI model; it does not tell benign from malignant)
